we have demonstrated gate-tunable negative resistance in a MoS2/h-BN/WSe2 device at room temperature.

The main takeaway from our work is that
NDR in Tungsten Diselenide (WTe2) is not only possible at room temperature but can be controlled by a back-gate, which is a crucial requirement for TFETs.
NDR is observed in a device where the tunneling current is dominated by the MoS2/WSe2 interface and not by the MoS 2/hBN interface.
the gate control of NDR in MoS2/WSe2 heterojunctions is possible, and the NDR is tunable with temperature.
